"Create a realistic open-world zombie survival game inspired by Dying Light.

The game should feature:

- Ultra-realistic 3D graphics.
- A large abandoned city with explorable buildings.
- Players can enter houses, apartments, shops and hospitals.
- Search rooms, cupboards, drawers and containers for useful supplies.
- Different types of zombies.
- Realistic weapons and combat.
- A complete survival system with health, stamina, hunger and inventory.
- Day and night cycles.
- Dynamic weather.
- Realistic animations and immersive sound effects.
- First-person gameplay.
- An atmospheric post-apocalyptic world.

Make exploration, looting and survival the main focus. The world should feel dangerous, realistic and immersive.
"

I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of.

Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does.

Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode.
====AGENTS====
# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'

export function projectType(root) {

export function rollLoot(type, rng, { min = 1, max = 3 } = {}) {
  const table = TABLES[type] || TABLES.kitchen
  const rolls = randInt(rng, min, max)
  const out = []
  for (let i = 0; i < rolls; i++) {
    for (const [id, qty, chance] of table) {
      if (rng() < chance) {
        const q = Math.max(1, Math.round(rand(rng, qty * 0.6, qty * 1.4)))
        out.push(stack(id, q))
        break
      }
    }
  }
  if (!out.length) out.push(stack('scrap', 1))
  // merge duplicate stacks
  const merged = []
  for (const s of out) {
    const ex = merged.find(m => m.id === s.id)
    if (ex) ex.qty += s.qty
    else merged.push({ ...s })
  }
  return merged
}

+  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- shells
+  buildShell({ cx, cz, w, d, h, facing = 1, doorX, doorW = 1.25, ceiling = 3.08, floor = 'wood', wall = 'wallpaper', wallColor = '#b6ac96', frontKey = 'plaster', frontColor = '#b4a892', backKey = 'plaster', backColor = '#a79b87', thickness = 0.34, doorLabel = 'Door', doorKind = 'wood', doorRotY = null, ceilColor = '#b0a89a', roofColor = '#746c5c', doorHeight = 2.32 }) {

+    base.vertexColors = true

+  }
+
+  addRoomLight(x, y, z, color, intensity = 12, distance = 8, type = 'bulb', flicker = 0) {

content.text:
Potential issues:
- `buildShell` adds a default room light for each building. I'll track light count later.
- Pharmacy `const frontZ = 9 * -1` unused; fine.
- Shell `wallXGap` usage: I call this.wallX(-17.75...) solid full wall then immediately wallXGap over the same wall, doubling geometry/colliders and no gap. Need remove solid wall call. I wrote:
```
this.wallX(-17.75, ... ) 
this.wallXGap(-17.75,...)
```
Remove first.
- Apartment interior partition door gaps: wallXGap with 3 gaps called multiple times; wallXGap builds segments between a/b, but each call separately builds segments only around its gap and the rest outside; calling 3 times on same wall duplicates large portions. E.g. call1 gap -9.4..-8.0 builds segments -13.5..-9.4 and -8..1.5; call2 builds -13.5..-3.5 and -2.1..1.5 (overlap) etc. Need a single function supporting multiple gaps. Let's implement `wallXGaps(z, x1,x2, height, thickness, gaps[])` and `wallZGaps`. Or avoid multiple: partition with 3 door gaps is uncommon; make 2. Better implement generic.

Add methods:
```
wallXWithGaps(z,x1,x2,h,t,key,color,gaps,opts)
```
gaps sorted; solid spans; lintels per gap. Same for Z.
Then replace apartment calls with one with gaps array. Also possible later use.

- `this.addStaticShelf(8.0, 12.0, 0, 4.2, ...)` static shelf along x 4.2 wide at z=12 - okay. But then market shelves overlap counters? fine.
- `addContainer` default table when table null uses type string, but for 'kitchen_cabinet' there's no table; rollLoot uses fallback kitchen. Fine. 'wardrobe' table exists, 'dresser' no table fallback kitchen (we passed nightstand). 'suitcase' fallback kitchen (we pass storage). Fine.
- `addContainer` for 'med_cabinet' wall-mounted at y=1.22: our colliders disabled, good. But group position y=1.22 and geometry local 0..; so bottom at 1.22, works.
- `addWindow` with `broken:true` and `lit:false` draws crack overlay; good.
- Front wall at z=8.96 for south facade? shell front wall center frontZ - facing*thickness/2. facing=-1, frontZ=minZ=9; center=9.17. Exterior face of wall at z=9.0? Wall extends 9.0..9.34. Windows at z=8.96 (street side) correct. Signs at 8.9 float slightly (0.06 from wall) good. For apartment windows at z=8.96 but door at x=-7 etc.
- `addWindowGrid` for south-facing row with front z=8.96 rotY=PI; correct.
- North pharmacy windows at -8.96: front wall exterior face at -9.0 (frontZ=-9). Windows at -8.96 (in front) correct.

- In buildApartment, `addIvyWall(2.05, ...)` east side wall x=2; okay.
- `addPipes(2.12,12.1,20.5, HALF_PI)` need define.

- AddBalcony, FireEscape, IvyWall, AC, Pipes methods to write.

- Hero building interior partitions need gaps. Let's implement wallXWithGaps now, replace apartment calls. Also pharmacy double wall.

- I referenced `this.addWindowGrid(6.6, 17.4, 8.96, -1, 4.2, 0, 3, 44)` floors=0 okay.

- Door labels etc.

Now part 4B: hospital/tenement/safehouse and helper methods for balconies, fire escapes, AC, pipes, ivy. Let's write.

Hospital:
- shell doorX=27, doorW=3.0. Door kind glass width 3 heavy, okay. Door label. BuildShell door frame posts at gx1/gx2. Good.
- Add canopy: columns at x=20,34? Entrance x=27, canopy width 10, depth 3.5 extending z=-6.5? Front at z=-9, sidewalk to -5.5, extend canopy to z=-6.2. Add columns at x=23,31 z=-6.4, y 0..3.6; slab at 3.7. Colliders for columns? add small colliders? Maybe yes but can annoy. Add boxes without colliders.
- Sign.
- Windows: floors 3, cols 8, baseY 4.6. Hospital facade pale.
- Emergency sign red cross, quarantine banner.
- Graffiti.
- Interior: wall at z=-19.5 with 3 gaps; vertical partitions x=21.2 and 31.8 from z -33.6..-19.5. Need wallZGaps for doors? We can use solid vertical partitions.
- Lobby reception desk.
- supply room shelf/cabinets/crates.
- surgery table, lights.
- ward beds.
- Lights: shell default at (cx+0.18w=32.2, 3.2, cz+...=-17?) actually cz + facing*d*0.18 = -21.5 + 4.5 = -17; good.
  Add supply cold flicker + ward red.
- Containers: 7.
- Spawns 2.
- Ambulance outside handled street props.

Tenement:
- shell, windows, balcony/fire escape, AC/pipes.
- interior partitions:
  - wallXGap(-16.5, -32.5, -13.5, gaps at -25..-23.6, -18..-16.8) => use wallXWithGaps.
  - wallZ(-23, -24.6, -16.5, ...) solid.
  - maybe kitchen/living open.
- Furniture.
- lights added by shell + flicker.
- containers.
- spawns.

Safehouse:
- shell, sign, barricade, UV lamp.
- interior with washers, counter, couch, cot, table, radio, safe locker.
- safe zone trigger and quest point.
- Add glowing green UV lamp + point light? shell default warm; add a purple/UV light? Use addRoomLight maybe adds another point. Could use emissive/glow only. Use emissive purple bar above door + glow no light; interior shell light warm.
- Add cardboard boxes, supplies.
- Safehouse containers.
- No spawns.

Helpers:
`addBalcony(x, y, z, w, depth, rotY)`:
- slab at y, position z outward. For facing south, z=8.35 and balcony extends toward 7.1. Slab box w x .12 x depth with center z - depth/2? rotY handling. Simpler parameterized with rotY and local placement; slab center at local z=+depth/2 from wall? We can just implement for south-facing front: using rotY=PI and local z? Let's generalize with local coordinates and rotY:
  group center at wall x,z; local +z points outward from facade. For south-facing (rotY=PI), local +z = -z (world) which is toward street. Good: outward = local +z. Slab local center (0,y,depth/2). Place at x,z with rotY. Railing at local z=depth, y+0.5: horizontal rails; posts.
- Add laundry on balcony: colored fabric planes hanging from rail, using batch plane with two sides. Rotated? Use simple boxes.
- Add potted plant.
- Collider? Balconies above head; no.
`addFireEscape(x,z,height)`: metal platform at y=4.2 and maybe 7.2; vertical ladders, railings. Decorative.
`addAC(x,y,z,rotY)`: metal box protruding from wall, fan.
`addPipes(x,z1,z2,rotY)`: vertical pipe with brackets along wall.
`addIvyWall(x,y,z,rotY,w,h,seed)`: a few transparent planes with ivy texture; batch key ivy; use UV.
`addLaundryLine` maybe in props.

Let's add wallXWithGaps first and helper methods in this chunk.

Wait `wallXWithGaps` signature (z,x1,x2,h,thickness,key,color,gaps,opts) but apartment call uses that order yes. `wallXGap` doesn't call multi: okay.

Now chunk 4B.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a playable first-person open-world zombie survival game inspired by Dying Light, emphasizing exploration, looting, and survival in an atmospheric abandoned city, using Three.js.

## Requirements
- Ultra-realistic 3D graphics; large explorable city with enterable houses, apartments, shops and hospitals.
- Search rooms, cupboards, drawers and containers for supplies.
- Multiple zombie types, realistic weapons/combat.
- Complete survival system: health, stamina, hunger, inventory.
- Day/night cycles, dynamic weather, realistic animations and immersive sound.
- First-person gameplay and atmospheric post-apocalyptic world.
- Exploration, looting and survival must be the main focus; world should feel dangerous, realistic and immersive.

## Decisions
- Self-contained Vite + Three.js 0.187 web game; fully procedural textures, geometry, and WebAudio assets (no external asset downloads).
- Title chosen: **DEAD HOUR**, set in Harbor City quarantine zone; start time ~17:19 golden hour.
- Gameplay starts at `(18, 1.65, 3.8)` looking west down Harbor Avenue; hospital on right, pharmacy ahead.
- Start menu includes a single `Play` button (capture auto-start regex-compatible); other menu buttons are `HOW TO PLAY` and `SETTINGS`.
- Fonts installed via `@fontsource/barlow-condensed` and `@fontsource/inter`.
- Quality strategy: merged geometry batches, selective dynamic shadows, post-processing bloom/grade, fog, procedural materials; target software/SwiftShader rendering.
- Loot flow: hover prompt → timed search → loot panel; inventory via Tab; start weapon `Worn Machete`.
- Quest: search Harbor Pharmacy for `antibiotics`, then deliver to The Old Laundry safehouse.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` with Vite/Three scripts, `index.html`, full `src/styles.css` HUD/menu/panels design.
- `src/utils.js`: RNG/noise helpers, `GeoBatch` geometry merging, UV scaling, blob textures.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural asphalt, sidewalk, concrete, plaster, brick, wood, metal, wallpaper, tile, carpet, windows, signs, posters, graffiti, blood, puddles, weeds, ivy, paper, hazard stripes, awning, dirt, smoke, muzzle flash.
- `src/items.js`: complete item registry, SVG icons, weapon stats, loot tables, `rollLoot`.
- `src/sky.js`: shader sky, sun/moon/clouds/stars, day-night cycle, weather state machine, lightning, rain particle system, dynamic lights, environment reflection refresh.
- `src/world.js` partially built (large file): materials, helpers, ground, building shells, doors, containers, furniture, pharmacy/apartment/market/hospital/tenement/safehouse interiors, filler buildings, backdrop/skyline, cables.

### Active
- Continuing `src/world.js` with `// @@PART6` marker before class closing brace.
- Remaining world methods: `buildStreetProps`, `buildAtmosphere`, `buildDecals`, `update`, `focus`, `interact`, `openDoor`, point-light culling, safe zones, dust, smoke animation.

### Blocked
- `world.js` is syntactically complete at current marker but references not-yet-defined methods only at runtime (`buildStreetProps`, `buildAtmosphere`, `buildDecals`) and helpers added later.
- No `src/main.js`, player, zombies, combat, UI controller, audio, or post-processing yet, so app cannot run.

## Next Move
1. Finish `src/world.js` part 6: street props (cars/bus/ambulance/police, barricades, lamps, wires, fires, dumpsters), atmosphere (dust motes, flames, smoke), decals, and `update/focus/interact/door` logic.
2. Create `src/player.js`: pointer lock, WASD/sprint/crouch/jump, collider resolution, head bob, stamina, footsteps, focus raycast.
3. Create `src/zombies.js`: procedural walker/infected/brute/screamer models, AI, attacks, damages, corpse loot.
4. Create `src/combat.js`: first-person viewmodels (machete, pipe, axe, pistol, shotgun, rifle), melee/ranged attacks, reload, recoil, muzzle flash, blood particles.
5. Create `src/ui.js` and `src/audio.js`: HUD, inventory/loot/pause/death panels, quest updates; procedural WebAudio ambience/weapons/zombies.
6. Create `src/main.js` + `src/post.js`: orchestrate menu/game, post FX, weather/quest/safehouse logic, render loop; verify with Playwright screenshots and iterate visuals.
7. Run `npm run build`, start dev server, capture 1440x900 screenshots, inspect for visual/gameplay defects.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: in-progress city/interiors/lootables; marker `// @@PART6`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sky.js`: sky/day-night/weather/rain system used by world/main.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: all procedural textures/signs/decals.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/items.js`: item definitions, loot tables, icons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/utils.js`: `GeoBatch`, RNG/noise, blob textures.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: complete UI styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: HUD, menu, panel DOM structure.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/package.json`: scripts `dev`, `build`, `preview`; dependencies.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`, `capture.sh`: runtime entry points, require built `index.html`.

## Important Context
- Build/deploy runtime requires static `index.html`; Vite config defaults are fine. `start.sh` uses `$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs` which runs `vite build --base ./`.
- Capture auto-start only clicks a visible enabled button whose text matches exactly `Play`, `Start`, `Start Game`, or `Play Now`; ensure only `PLAY` matches.
- Screenshot capture waits ~1s after clicking; world must be prebuilt before present so gameplay renders immediately.
- Key world coordinates: pharmacy center `(1,-15.5)` front `z=-9`, hospital center `(27,-21.5)`, apartment `(-6,17)`, market `(12,14.5)`, tenement `(-23,-17)`, safehouse `(-27,14.5)`; main street `z=0`, width 11; cross street x 44–56.
- Intro view expects pharmacy quest point `world.questPoints.pharmacy`, safehouse marker `world.questPoints.safehouse`.
- World currently creates ~11 point lights; plan dynamic culling to nearest ~5 to control SwiftShader cost.
- `GeoBatch` materials must be registered with `B.use(key, material)` before `build()`; `makeMaterials()` already registers all material keys plus `lit1`–`lit4`.
- Known fixes applied: door hinges offset and panels shifted to pivot correctly; three-gap apartment partition uses `wallXWithGaps`; invalid `addStaticShelf` line removed.
- No commits made yet; all work is uncommitted in the working tree.

87: export function rollLoot(type, rng, { min = 1, max = 3 } = {}) {
88:   const table = TABLES[type] || TABLES.kitchen
89:   const rolls = randInt(rng, min, max)
90:   const out = []
91:   for (let i = 0; i < rolls; i++) {
92:     for (const [id, qty, chance] of table) {
93:       if (rng() < chance) {
94:         const q = Math.max(1, Math.round(rand(rng, qty * 0.6, qty * 1.4)))
95:         out.push(stack(id, q))
96:         break
97:       }
98:     }
99:   }
100:   if (!out.length) out.push(stack('scrap', 1))
101:   // merge duplicate stacks
102:   const merged = []
103:   for (const s of out) {
104:     const ex = merged.find(m => m.id === s.id)
105:     if (ex) ex.qty += s.qty
106:     else merged.push({ ...s })
107:   }
108:   return merged
109: }

+      }

+    // warning paint on the asphalt

+  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- runtime
+  update(dt, elapsed, playerPos, cameraPos) {

+    for (const door of this.doors) {

+    // flames

+      c.rotation.y = -u.phase + HALF_PI

+    }

+    if (playerPos && this.pointLights.length) {
+      this._lightTimer = (this._lightTimer ?? 0) - dt
+      if (this._lightTimer <= 0) {
+        this._lightTimer = 0.35
+        const scored = this.pointLights.map(l => ({
+          l, d: (l.position.x - playerPos.x) ** 2 + (l.position.z - playerPos.z) ** 2
+        })).sort((a, b) => a.d - b.d)
+        const budget = 7
+        for (let i = 0; i < scored.length; i++) scored[i].l.visible = i < budget
+      }
+    }
+  }
+
+  // nearest interactable under the crosshair
+  focus(camera, maxDistance = 3.4) {
+    if (!camera || !this.interactRoots.length) {
+      if (this.focusRecord) this.highlightContainer(this.focusRecord.container, false)
+      this.focusRecord = null
+      return null
+    }
+    this._ray.setFromCamera({ x: 0, y: 0 }, camera)
+    this._ray.far = maxDistance
+    const hits = this._ray.intersectObjects(this.interactRoots, true)
+    let rec = null
+    for (const h of hits) {
+      const r = h.object.userData.interact
+      if (r) { rec = r; break }
+    }
+    if (rec !== this.focusRecord) {
+      if (this.focusRecord) this.highlightContainer(this.focusRecord.container, false)
+      if (rec) this.highlightContainer(rec.container, true)
+      this.focusRecord = rec
+    }
+    return rec
+  }
+
+  interact(rec) {
+    if (!rec) return null
+    if (rec.type === 'door') {
+      const d = rec.door
+      if (!d) return null
+      if (d.locked) return { type: 'locked', label: d.label }
+      d.open = !d.open
+      return { type: 'door', open: d.open, label: d.label }
+    }
+    if (rec.type === 'container') {
+      const c = rec.container
+      if (!c) return null
+      if (c.searched) return { type: 'empty', label: c.name }
+      c.searched = true
+      rec.action = 'SEARCHED'
+      if (c.material) {
+        c.material.emissive.set('#000000')
+        c.material.emissiveIntensity = 0
+      }
+      const loot = c.loot.map(s => ({ ...s }))
+      c.loot = []
+      return { type: 'loot', label: c.name, loot }
+    }
+    return null
+  }
+
+  inSafeZone(pos) {
+    for (const z of this.safeZones) {
+      if ((pos.x - z.x) ** 2 + (pos.z - z.z) ** 2 < z.r * z.r) return z
+    }
+    return null
+  }
+
+  nearestQuest(key, pos) {
+    const p = this.questPoints[key]
+    if (!p) return null
+    return { point: p, distance: Math.hypot(p.x - pos.x, p.z - pos.z) }
+  }
+
+  dispose() {
+    this.scene.remove(this.root)
+  }
 }

import { clamp, lerp, mulberry32 } from './utils.js'

export class AudioEngine {
  constructor() {
    this.ctx = null
    this.ready = false
    this.master = null
    this.volume = 0.72
    this.rng = mulberry32(5150)
    this.weather = { rain: 0, overcast: 0.2 }
    this.creakTimer = 6
    this.moanTimer = 9
    this.heartTimer = 0
    this.lastStep = 0
    this.enabled = false
    this.playing = false
  }

  init() {
    if (this.ctx) { this.ctx.resume?.(); return }
    const AC = window.AudioContext || window.webkitAudioContext
    if (!AC) return
    this.ctx = new AC()
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const comp = ctx.createDynamicsCompressor()
    comp.threshold.value = -18
    comp.knee.value = 22
    comp.ratio.value = 4
    comp.attack.value = 0.004
    comp.release.value = 0.22
    this.master = ctx.createGain()
    this.master.gain.value = this.volume
    this.master.connect(comp)
    comp.connect(ctx.destination)
    this.comp = comp

    // white noise buffer
    const len = ctx.sampleRate * 2
    const buf = ctx.createBuffer(1, len, ctx.sampleRate)
    const data = buf.getChannelData(0)
    for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) data[i] = Math.random() * 2 - 1
    this.noiseBuffer = buf

    // brown-ish noise for wind
    const windBuf = ctx.createBuffer(1, len, ctx.sampleRate)
    const wd = windBuf.getChannelData(0)
    let last = 0
    for (let i = 0; i < len; i++) {
      last = last * 0.985 + (Math.random() * 2 - 1) * 0.015
      wd[i] = last * 3.2
    }
    this.windBuffer = windBuf

    this.buildAmbience()
    this.ready = true
    this.enabled = true
  }

  buildAmbience() {
    const ctx = this.ctx
    // wind layer
    const wind = ctx.createBufferSource()
    wind.buffer = this.windBuffer
    wind.loop = true
    const windFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    windFilter.type = 'lowpass'
    windFilter.frequency.value = 380
    windFilter.Q.value = 0.6
    this.windGain = ctx.createGain()
    this.windGain.gain.value = 0.001
    wind.connect(windFilter)
    windFilter.connect(this.windGain)
    this.windGain.connect(this.master)
    wind.start()
    this.wind = wind

    // high airy layer
    const air = ctx.createBufferSource()
    air.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    air.loop = true
    const airFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    airFilter.type = 'bandpass'
    airFilter.frequency.value = 1400
    airFilter.Q.value = 0.35
    this.airGain = ctx.createGain()
    this.airGain.gain.value = 0.0001
    air.connect(airFilter)
    airFilter.connect(this.airGain)
    this.airGain.connect(this.master)
    air.start()
    this.air = air

    // rain layer
    const rain = ctx.createBufferSource()
    rain.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    rain.loop = true
    const rainFilter = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    rainFilter.type = 'highpass'
    rainFilter.frequency.value = 1500
    this.rainFilter = rainFilter
    this.rainGain = ctx.createGain()
    this.rainGain.gain.value = 0
    rain.connect(rainFilter)
    rainFilter.connect(this.rainGain)
    this.rainGain.connect(this.master)
    rain.start()
    this.rain = rain

    // low drone bed
    const droneGain = ctx.createGain()
    droneGain.gain.value = 0.038
    droneGain.connect(this.master)
    this.droneGain = droneGain
    for (const [f, type, g] of [[41.2, 'sine', 0.6], [61.7, 'triangle', 0.32], [82.4, 'sine', 0.18]]) {
      const o = ctx.createOscillator()
      o.type = type
      o.frequency.value = f
      const gn = ctx.createGain()
      gn.gain.value = g
      const filt = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
      filt.type = 'lowpass'
      filt.frequency.value = 220
      o.connect(filt)
      filt.connect(gn)
      gn.connect(droneGain)
      o.start()
      // slow drift
      const lfo = ctx.createOscillator()
      lfo.frequency.value = 0.03 + this.rng() * 0.05
      const lfoGain = ctx.createGain()
      lfoGain.gain.value = 0.6
      lfo.connect(lfoGain)
      lfoGain.connect(o.frequency)
      lfo.start()
    }
  }

  resume() {
    if (this.ctx?.state === 'suspended') this.ctx.resume()
  }

  setVolume(v) {
    this.volume = clamp(v, 0, 1)
    if (this.master) this.master.gain.value = this.volume
  }

  setWeather({ rain = 0, overcast = 0.2 } = {}) {
    this.weather = { rain, overcast }
    if (!this.ready) return
    const t = this.ctx.currentTime
    this.rainGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(rain * 0.05, t, 0.8)
    this.rainFilter.frequency.setTargetAtTime(1000 + rain * 1800, t, 0.8)
    this.windGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(0.016 + overcast * 0.026, t, 1.2)
    this.airGain.gain.setTargetAtTime(0.0016 + overcast * 0.004, t, 1.2)
  }

  panFor(pos, camera, yaw) {
    if (!pos) return { pan: 0, vol: 1, dist: 0 }
    const dx = pos.x - camera.x
    const dz = pos.z - camera.z
    const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dz)
    const rx = Math.cos(yaw), rz = -Math.sin(yaw)
    const pan = clamp((dx * rx + dz * rz) / Math.max(1, dist), -1, 1) * 0.85
    const vol = clamp(1 / (1 + dist * 0.11), 0, 1)
    return { pan, vol, dist }
  }

  connectOutput(node, pan = 0, gain = 1) {
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const g = ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.value = gain
    let out = g
    if (ctx.createStereoPanner) {
      const p = ctx.createStereoPanner()
      p.pan.value = pan
      g.connect(p)
      out = p
    }
    out.connect(this.master)
    node.connect(g)
    return g
  }

  noise(duration, { type = 'bandpass', freq = 800, q = 0.8, gain = 0.3, pan = 0, attack = 0.002, sweepTo = null } = {}) {
    if (!this.ready) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const src = ctx.createBufferSource()
    src.buffer = this.noiseBuffer
    src.loop = true
    const filt = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    filt.type = type
    filt.frequency.value = freq
    filt.Q.value = q
    if (sweepTo) filt.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(40, sweepTo), ctx.currentTime + duration)
    const g = ctx.createGain()
    const now = ctx.currentTime
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.0002, gain), now + attack)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + duration)
    src.connect(filt)
    filt.connect(g)
    this.connectOutput(g, pan)
    src.start(now, this.rng() * 1.5)
    src.stop(now + duration + 0.02)
  }

  tone(freq, duration, { type = 'sine', gain = 0.2, pan = 0, glide = null, attack = 0.004, delay = 0 } = {}) {
    if (!this.ready) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const o = ctx.createOscillator()
    o.type = type
    const now = ctx.currentTime + delay
    o.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, now)
    if (glide) o.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(20, glide), now + duration)
    const g = ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(Math.max(0.0002, gain), now + attack)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + duration)
    o.connect(g)
    this.connectOutput(g, pan)
    o.start(now)
    o.stop(now + duration + 0.02)
  }

  play(name, opts = {}) {
    if (!this.ready || !this.enabled) return
    const pan = opts.pan ?? 0
    switch (name) {
      case 'footstep': {
        const s = opts.surface || 'stone'
        const vol = (opts.volume ?? 0.6) * 0.55
        if (s === 'interior') {
          this.noise(0.11, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 320 + this.rng() * 160, q: 1.4, gain: vol * 0.75, pan })
          this.tone(72 + this.rng() * 22, 0.11, { type: 'sine', gain: vol * 0.4, pan })
        } else if (s === 'asphalt') {
          this.noise(0.1, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 700 + this.rng() * 500, q: 0.8, gain: vol * 0.62, pan })
          this.tone(96, 0.08, { type: 'sine', gain: vol * 0.22, pan })
        } else {
          this.noise(0.09, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 1150 + this.rng() * 600, q: 1.1, gain: vol * 0.5, pan })
        }
        break
      }
      case 'swing':
        this.noise(0.24, { type: 'bandpass', freq: opts.heavy ? 320 : 520, q: 1.1, gain: opts.heavy ? 0.36 : 0.24, pan, sweepTo: opts.heavy ? 140 : 1800, attack: 0.03 })
        break
      case 'bladeHit':
        this.noise(0.16, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 1050, q: 1.4, gain: 0.4, pan })
        this.tone(120, 0.16, { type: 'square', gain: 0.1, pan, glide: 55 })
        this.noise(0.09, { type: 'highpass', freq: 2400, gain: 0.16, pan })
        break
      case 'bluntHit':
        this.tone(74, 0.24, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.42, pan, glide: 36 })
        this.noise(0.18, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 550, q: 1.2, gain: 0.34, pan })
        break
      case 'pistol':
        this.noise(0.17, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 2600, q: 0.9, gain: 0.7, pan, attack: 0.001, sweepTo: 260 })
        this.tone(155, 0.2, { type: 'square', gain: 0.3, pan, glide: 45 })
        this.tone(70, 0.26, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.42, pan, glide: 34 })
        this.noise(0.5, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 600, q: 0.6, gain: 0.12, pan })
        break
      case 'shotgun':
        this.noise(0.32, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 2100, q: 0.7, gain: 0.9, pan, attack: 0.001, sweepTo: 170 })
        this.tone(92, 0.36, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.55, pan, glide: 28 })
        this.noise(0.9, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 480, q: 0.5, gain: 0.16, pan })
        break
      case 'rifle':
        this.noise(0.2, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 3200, q: 0.8, gain: 0.8, pan, attack: 0.001, sweepTo: 300 })
        this.tone(180, 0.18, { type: 'square', gain: 0.25, pan, glide: 50 })
        this.tone(64, 0.3, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.4, pan, glide: 30 })
        break
      case 'dryfire':
        this.noise(0.035, { type: 'highpass', freq: 2200, gain: 0.16, pan })
        this.tone(1600, 0.03, { type: 'square', gain: 0.04, pan })
        break
      case 'reload':
        this.noise(0.05, { type: 'highpass', freq: 2600, gain: 0.16, pan })
        this.tone(280, 0.06, { type: 'square', gain: 0.05, pan, delay: 0.05 })
        this.noise(0.06, { type: 'highpass', freq: 1800, gain: 0.15, pan: pan + 0.2, delay: 0.35 })
        this.tone(180, 0.05, { type: 'square', gain: 0.05, pan, delay: 0.5 })
        break
      case 'impact':
        this.noise(0.06, { type: opts.surface === 'ground' ? 'lowpass' : 'bandpass', freq: opts.surface === 'ground' ? 500 : 1800, q: 1.2, gain: 0.14, pan })
        break
      case 'hurt':
        this.tone(66, 0.28, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.34, pan, glide: 38 })
        this.noise(0.2, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 420, q: 1, gain: 0.24, pan })
        break
      case 'groan':
        this.groan(pan, opts.vol ?? 0.5, false)
        break
      case 'scream':
        this.scream(pan, opts.vol ?? 0.55)
        break
      case 'kill':
        this.tone(88, 0.4, { type: 'sawtooth', gain: 0.18, pan, glide: 41 })
        this.noise(0.3, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 380, q: 1.4, gain: 0.22, pan })
        break
      case 'pickup':
        this.tone(620, 0.08, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.1, pan })
        this.tone(880, 0.12, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.08, pan, delay: 0.06 })
        break
      case 'click':
        this.tone(420, 0.04, { type: 'square', gain: 0.05, pan })
        break
      case 'door':
        this.noise(0.5, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 240, q: 2.2, gain: 0.18, pan, sweepTo: 120, attack: 0.05 })
        break
      case 'quest':
        this.tone(392, 0.6, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.14, pan })
        this.tone(523.25, 0.7, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.11, pan, delay: 0.14 })
        this.tone(659.25, 0.9, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.09, pan, delay: 0.3 })
        break
      case 'pickupGun':
        this.noise(0.08, { type: 'highpass', freq: 1400, gain: 0.14, pan })
        this.tone(340, 0.1, { type: 'square', gain: 0.06, pan })
        break
      case 'heartbeat':
        this.tone(48, 0.19, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.4, pan })
        this.tone(42, 0.22, { type: 'sine', gain: 0.3, pan, delay: 0.24 })
        break
      case 'lightning':
        this.noise(1.4, { type: 'lowpass', freq: 420, q: 0.5, gain: 0.35, pan: (this.rng() - 0.5) * 1.4, attack: 0.06 })
        break
    }
  }

  groan(pan = 0, vol = 0.4, distant = false) {
    if (!this.ready) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const now = ctx.currentTime
    const dur = 0.9 + this.rng() * 1.1
    const base = 58 + this.rng() * 46
    const g = ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(vol * 0.14, now + 0.15)
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(vol * 0.14, now + dur * 0.6)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + dur)
    const filt = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    filt.type = 'bandpass'
    filt.frequency.value = 340 + this.rng() * 260
    filt.Q.value = 3.2
    const o = ctx.createOscillator()
    o.type = 'sawtooth'
    o.frequency.setValueAtTime(base, now)
    o.frequency.linearRampToValueAtTime(base * (0.8 + this.rng() * 0.5), now + dur)
    const lfo = ctx.createOscillator()
    lfo.frequency.value = 5 + this.rng() * 4
    const lg = ctx.createGain()
    lg.gain.value = 12
    lfo.connect(lg)
    lg.connect(o.frequency)
    o.connect(filt)
    filt.connect(g)
    this.connectOutput(g, pan, distant ? 0.55 : 1)
    o.start(now)
    lfo.start(now)
    o.stop(now + dur + 0.05)
    lfo.stop(now + dur + 0.05)
    if (!distant) this.noise(dur * 0.7, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 600, q: 2, gain: vol * 0.03, pan })
  }

  scream(pan = 0, vol = 0.5) {
    if (!this.ready) return
    const ctx = this.ctx
    const now = ctx.currentTime
    const dur = 1.8
    const g = ctx.createGain()
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(0.0001, now)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(vol * 0.2, now + 0.1)
    g.gain.setValueAtTime(vol * 0.2, now + dur * 0.55)
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001, now + dur)
    const o = ctx.createOscillator()
    o.type = 'sawtooth'
    o.frequency.setValueAtTime(340, now)
    o.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(900, now + 0.35)
    o.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(480, now + dur * 0.8)
    const o2 = ctx.createOscillator()
    o2.type = 'square'
    o2.frequency.setValueAtTime(510, now)
    o2.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(760, now + 0.3)
    o2.frequency.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(390, now + dur * 0.8)
    const filt = ctx.createBiquadFilter()
    filt.type = 'bandpass'
    filt.frequency.value = 1300
    filt.Q.value = 1.2
    o.connect(filt)
    o2.connect(filt)
    filt.connect(g)
    this.connectOutput(g, pan)
    o.start(now); o2.start(now)
    o.stop(now + dur); o2.stop(now + dur)
    this.noise(dur * 0.7, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 1600, q: 1.2, gain: 0.05, pan })
  }

  update(dt, state = {}) {
    if (!this.ready) return
    const { playing, player, sky, camera, yaw } = state
    if (!playing) {
      this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(this.volume * 0.45, this.ctx.currentTime, 0.5)
      return
    }
    this.master.gain.setTargetAtTime(this.volume, this.ctx.currentTime, 0.4)
    this.creakTimer -= dt
    this.moanTimer -= dt
    if (this.creakTimer <= 0) {
      this.creakTimer = 9 + this.rng() * 18
      const pan = (this.rng() - 0.5) * 1.5
      if (this.rng() < 0.55) {
        this.noise(0.7 + this.rng() * 0.7, { type: 'bandpass', freq: 190 + this.rng() * 300, q: 4, gain: 0.055, pan, attack: 0.08, sweepTo: 120 })
      } else {
        this.tone(220 + this.rng() * 160, 0.5, { type: 'triangle', gain: 0.025, pan, glide: 180 })
      }
    }
    if (this.moanTimer <= 0) {
      this.moanTimer = 14 + this.rng() * 24
      this.groan((this.rng() - 0.5) * 1.3, 0.28, true)
    }
    if (player && player.health < 38 && player.alive) {
      this.heartTimer -= dt
      if (this.heartTimer <= 0) {
        this.heartTimer = 0.8 + player.health / 60
        this.play('heartbeat')
      }
    }
    if (sky) {
      const rain = sky.rainAmount || 0
      const over = sky.overcast || 0.2
      if (Math.abs(rain - this.weather.rain) > 0.02 || Math.abs(over - this.weather.overcast) > 0.05) {
        this.setWeather({ rain, overcast: over })
      }
    }
  }

  playAt(name, position, camera, yaw, opts = {}) {
    const { pan, vol, dist } = this.panFor(position, camera, yaw)
    if (dist > 42) return
    this.play(name, { ...opts, pan, vol: vol * (opts.vol ?? 1) })
  }
}

Now UI. This is large. Let's design the UI interactions carefully.

DOM ids available. We'll create UI class with references.

Responsibilities:
- Start menu: on Play click -> game.start()
- How To Play, Settings: open overlay panel with HTML.
- HUD update.
- Inventory panel via Tab.
- Loot panel.
- Pause panel.
- Death screen.
- Interaction prompt + hold-to-search.
- Quest updates.
- Toasts.
- Compass.
- Quickbar.

Game interfaces:
- `game.playing` bool, `game.paused` bool.
- `game.panelOpen` maybe UI state.
- `game.start()`, `game.pause()`, `game.resume()`, `game.restart()`, `game.quitToMenu()`.
- `game.inventory`, `game.combat`, `game.world`, `game.player`, `game.sky`, `game.zombies`, `game.audio`.
- `game.quest` object {stage, target, title, sub, completed}.
- `game.ui`.

UI state:
- `this.screen = 'menu' | 'game'`.
- panel open for inventory/loot/pause/howto/settings. Use #panel and #panel-frame. Hide by class hidden.
- When panel opens: game.setPaused(true), player.unlock(), but reopening after close should re-lock.
- Need careful: pointerlockchange caused by opening panel triggers onLockChange in player; main may interpret; we'll manage via game.onPointerLockChange callback rather than UI. Simpler: UI.openPanel() calls game.setPaused(true) and player.unlock(); closing calls game.setPaused(false) and player.lock() (user gesture from button click works). Esc closes panel.
- Esc while playing: pointer lock lost -> browser fires pointerlockchange; main handles: if playing && !paused && !panelOpen -> open pause. But clicking Play locks pointer, fine. When player presses Esc browser exits pointer lock; main shows pause panel. Good.
- If pointer lock request fails in headless after Play, we don't want pause panel to show. On Play we call lock; if not locked after 200ms, keep playing (mouse look won't work but capture works). We should not auto-pause on initial failure. Only auto-pause on lock loss after having been locked. Track `game.hadLock`.

Search flow:
- UI binds keydown E? Player has focus. In update, if game playing & not paused and player.focus exists and E key pressed (player.keys.KeyE) -> progress += dt/duration; else decay.
- On completion: `const result = world.interact(rec)`; if loot and loot.length openLoot(result); if empty toast; if door play sound.
- Door should open on single press, not hold. So if rec.type==='door' and E pressed once (keydown event) -> interact immediately. Use keydown listener in UI for KeyE: if focus door -> interact. For containers, start hold. We'll bind UI keydown for E; set `this.eHeld=true`; update progress. On keyup false.
- Ring: #ring-progress stroke-dashoffset from 119 to 0.
- Interact prompt: action from rec.action, target rec.label. For searched containers action 'SEARCHED' and maybe no prompt? Still show 'EMPTY'. Show prompt if focus always.

Loot panel:
- Build HTML with cards. Each card click adds item to inventory (one qty? entire stack). On add success, remove from loot list; toast; play pickup. If failed (weight) toast danger.
- If item quest antibiotics, update quest stage when picked. `game.onLoot(id)`.
- 'TAKE ALL' button adds all possible. 'LEAVE' closes. If all taken, auto close? Keep open with "EMPTY".
- While loot panel open, game paused. Closing re-locks.

Inventory:
- Grid 8 columns of slots (slots length <= 32). Details pane for selected. Actions: EQUIP/USE, DROP, REPAIR.
- Use consumables: apply to player, remove item, close? Keep panel open and refresh. Use effects: health, hunger, thirst, stamina, infection cure? antibiotics is quest. Medkit etc. Also `repair` requires equipped weapon and adds condition.
- Weight display.
- Tab toggles. Key events: Tab, Escape, I? Use Tab.
- Quickbar: weapons first 4, then consumables [bandage, water, canned_food, flare]. Click slot equips/uses. Keys handled: combat 1-4; UI 5-8 use. Add listener.
- Weapon panel: name, ammo, reserve, condition, type.

HUD:
- Quest title/sub from game.quest. Distance computed to target point.
- Compass: determine heading angle from yaw. Strip transform translateX. The strip has 8 spans with gap 55. Simpler set text of compass-head and degree; animate strip by yaw. Let's compute heading degrees = ((-yaw*180/PI) % 360 + 360) % 360? Camera yaw PI/2 means facing west = 270°. Compass heading convention N=0, E=90, S=180, W=270. Our forward = (-sin yaw, -cos yaw). For yaw=0 forward -z = north. So heading = (-yaw*180/PI) mod 360. For yaw=PI/2 => -90 => 270 = west. Good.
- Strip: map heading to translateX around center. Spans order W,NW,N,NE,E,SE,S,SW. That's weird but we can just move strip based on -heading*2 px. Set head letter from 8 directions. degree 3-digit.
- Quest marker arrow on compass? There's compass-marker static center; could offset marker to target bearing. Nice: set left % based on relative bearing to quest target. Use marker style left = 50% + delta/2? We'll approximate. Also add class off if behind? Keep simple.
- Clock: sky.clockString(), day, weather label, temp (derive from time), dial fill (time/24*100), hand left.
- Weather icons map.
- Noise bars: player.noise * 8; toggle .on for bars <= level, hot if >0.7.
- Crosshair: aiming class, melee class. Hitmarker.
- Damage vignette: on hurt flash class; low health class.
- Subtitle queue.

Notifications:
- `toast(title, sub, kind)` creates .toast element in #notifications, auto remove after 4s; max 4.
- `mini(text)` in #toast-layer.

Quest logic:
- Method `setQuest(title, sub, targetVec, stage)`.
- In update, distance to target; update sub text e.g. "Harbor Pharmacy · 42 m".
- `game.onLoot(id)`: if id==='antibiotics' and stage 0 -> stage 1, set quest deliver, toast "Antibiotics recovered".
- If at safehouse (distance < 4) and stage 1 -> stage 2 complete, toast, audio quest, maybe spawn reward (bandage/medkit). We can call game.completeQuest().
- After complete, new objective "Scavenge Harbor General" target hospital? Might conflict with story. Maybe complete is enough, then objective "Survive the night" with no target. Game still playable.

Menu status: after world ready set ready. UI startup: menu visible, HUD hidden.

Panels HTML builder uses icons from items.js. import { ITEMS, iconSVG }.

Settings: quality select; sensitivity slider? Use option buttons Low/Balanced/High; toggles for bloom, subtitles. Store in game.settings. Quality changes can call game.applySettings(). Add resolution scale? Keep quality.

How to play: controls sheet and tips.

Pause: Resume, Inventory, How to Play, Settings, Quit to Menu. Buttons.

Death: create `.death-screen` appended to #app with stats and buttons "TRY AGAIN" and "MAIN MENU". Game handles respawn.

Pointer lock overlay? If not locked and playing but not paused, clicking canvas re-locks. Add click handler on canvas when playing & !locked & !paused -> player.lock().

Also show "CLICK TO LOOK" hint if not locked? Could add mini toast. Skip.

Let's write ui.js. Be careful with HTML and event delegation.

Need to avoid `Tab` default when panel. global keydown handles.

Also game.inventory.onChange = () => ui.refreshQuickbar + refresh weapon.

UI update should be efficient; DOM updates each frame at 60fps okay but we can throttle to 10Hz for text. But smooth bars each frame. Use requestAnimationFrame integrated in game loop.

Time format from sky.

Weather labels: clear 'CLEAR SKIES', haze 'LIGHT HAZE', overcast 'OVERCAST', rain 'RAIN', storm 'STORM'. Temp based on time: 18-28.

Interaction progress: duration by container type: corpse 1.15, med cabinet .8, safe .9, crate 1.0, etc. Search ring.

When opening loot, exit pointer lock. `this.openPanel('loot', html, {onClose})`.

Panel close handling: closePanel() hides #panel, set game.paused=false, player.lock() unless death/menu.

Esc key: if panel open -> closePanel (except death); else if playing -> game.pause() (open pause). But escape also exits pointer lock and triggers pointerlockchange. Need avoid double. In main on pointerlockchange when playing & !hadLock and no panel -> open pause. UI keydown Esc may also open. Guard if panel already open.

Let's implement `UI.openPause()` idempotent.

One concern: auto-capture clicks Play; pointer lock may or may not be granted. Screenshot after 1s. HUD should be visible. If pointer lock request throws/denied and main auto-pauses, we'd see pause overlay in screenshot — bad. So only auto-pause when `game.hadPointerLock` true and then lost. We'll implement in main.

UI start: hide menu .out then hidden after transition.

Now write.
Now the HUD, menus, panels, and loot flow.

Bug in takeAllLoot: `inv.add` loop logic is wrong: `for (let i=1;i<=s.qty;i++) if (inv.add(s.id,1)) qty=i` — if add fails once, later i may still success? As weight grows, once full later fails; qty ends as last success. But partial added already; fine. However `inv.remove(s.id,0)` is harmless. If `inv.add(s.id,s.qty)` fails, we attempt one by one; but if it partially added some? add returns false without adding anything when canAdd fails. Good. ## Objective
- Build a playable first-person open-world zombie survival game inspired by Dying Light, emphasizing exploration, looting, and survival in an atmospheric abandoned city, using Three.js.

## Requirements
- Ultra-realistic 3D graphics; large explorable city with enterable houses, apartments, shops and hospitals.
- Search rooms, cupboards, drawers and containers for supplies.
- Multiple zombie types, realistic weapons/combat.
- Complete survival system: health, stamina, hunger, inventory.
- Day/night cycles, dynamic weather, realistic animations and immersive sound.
- First-person gameplay and atmospheric post-apocalyptic world.
- Exploration, looting and survival must be the main focus; world should feel dangerous, realistic and immersive.

## Decisions
- Self-contained Vite + Three.js 0.187 web game; fully procedural textures, geometry, and WebAudio assets (no external asset downloads).
- Title: **DEAD HOUR**, set in Harbor City quarantine zone; start time ~17:19 golden hour.
- Gameplay starts at `(18, 1.65, 3.8)` looking west down Harbor Avenue; hospital on right, pharmacy ahead.
- Start menu includes a single `Play` button (capture auto-start regex-compatible); other menu buttons are `HOW TO PLAY` and `SETTINGS`.
- Fonts installed via `@fontsource/barlow-condensed` and `@fontsource/inter`.
- Quality strategy: merged geometry batches, selective dynamic shadows, post-processing bloom/grade, fog, procedural materials; target software/SwiftShader rendering.
- Loot flow: hover prompt → timed search → loot panel; inventory via Tab; start weapon `Worn Machete`.
- Quest: search Harbor Pharmacy for `antibiotics`, then deliver to The Old Laundry safehouse.
- Combat viewmodel rendered via separate `viewScene`/`viewCamera` after main render with `clearDepth`, so weapons self-occlude and stay on top of world geometry.
- Weapons/ammo spread across lootable containers (e.g., rifle in military crate, pistol in safehouse locker) rather than world enemies.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold: `package.json` with Vite/Three scripts, `index.html`, full `src/styles.css` HUD/menu/panel design.
- `src/utils.js`: RNG/noise helpers, `GeoBatch` geometry merging, UV scaling, blob textures.
- `src/textures.js`: procedural asphalt, sidewalk, concrete, plaster, brick, wood, metal, wallpaper, tile, carpet, windows, signs, posters, graffiti, blood, puddles, weeds, ivy, paper, hazard stripes, awning, dirt, smoke, muzzle flash.
- `src/items.js`: item registry, SVG icons, weapon stats, loot tables, `rollLoot`.
- `src/sky.js`: shader sky, sun/moon/clouds/stars, day-night cycle, weather state machine, lightning, rain, dynamic lights, environment reflection refresh.
- `src/world.js` complete: ground, hero interiors, filler city, backdrop, street props (vehicles, bus, ambulance, checkpoint, lamps, fires, dumpsters, tents, stalls), atmosphere (dust, steam, embers, crows), decals, point-light culling, doors, containers, focus/interact, safe zones, quest points, post-build corpse decal fallback.
- `src/player.js`: pointer lock, WASD/sprint/crouch/jump, collider resolution, head bob, stamina/hunger/thirst/infection, footsteps, focus raycast, camera shake, respawn, safe-zone healing.
- `src/zombies.js`: procedural walker/infected/brute/screamer models, AI states/wander/chase/attack, LOS blocking, damage/headshots, blood particles, death corpse loot, alert/scream/groan events, spawn refresh.
- `src/inventory.js`: stacking, weight limit, equip, condition/repair, weapon list.
- `src/combat.js`: procedural viewmodels for machete/knife/pipe/axe/pistol/shotgun/rifle, melee swings, hitscan guns, spread/pellets, magazines/reload, recoil, muzzle flash/light, impact particles, ADS/FOV, weapon switching, condition wear.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ambience (wind/air/rain/drone), footsteps, swings, impacts, guns, reload, groans, screams, heartbeat, quest chime, positional panning, weather-driven mix.
- `src/ui.js`: menu/start flow, HUD vitals/compass/clock/weather/quest distance, hold-E search ring, loot panel, inventory panel, pause/how-to/settings panels, death screen, toasts, subtitles, quickbar, hitmarkers, damage flash.
- `src/post.js`: EffectComposer with RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, custom grade ShaderPass (chromatic aberration, desaturation, warmth, vignette, grain, scanlines, damage tint), OutputPass; quality/bloom/size controls.

### Active
- Creating `src/main.js` to orchestrate renderer/scene/camera, sky/world/player/zombies/inventory/audio/UI/combat/post, menu-to-game transition, quest logic, weather, input/pointer-lock handling, resize, render loop, and weapon overlay rendering.
- Wire UI callbacks to game methods: `start`, `setPaused`, `restart`, `quitToMenu`, `setSetting`, `stats`, `onLoot`, `applySettings`, `addTrauma`.

### Blocked
- App cannot run until `src/main.js` exists and all cross-module APIs are wired.
- Known integration checks pending: `combat.muzzleFlash` should call `root.updateMatrixWorld(true)` and remove erroneous `viewScene.localToWorld`; `combat.meleeHit` reads `this.condition` but should use `this.inventory.condition`; `ui.takeAllLoot` partial-stack logic is awkward but functional.
- No `npm run build` or browser verification has been performed since adding player/zombies/combat/UI/audio/post.

## Next Move
1. Create `src/main.js` with game state, renderer, scene/camera, module instantiation order (`inventory` → `audio` → `ui` → `combat`), menu/Play start, pause/pointer-lock handling, resize, and the frame loop.
2. Implement quest progression in main/UI: pharmacy stage → antibiotics loot → safehouse delivery → completion; update quest points/distances and toasts.
3. Wire weather/rain/lightning to audio and sky; apply settings (quality, render scale, bloom, sensitivity, subtitles) and persist to localStorage.
4. Render pipeline: post-FX main scene, then `combat.render()` weapon overlay; ensure renderer size/DPR/pixel-ratio and viewCamera aspect match.
5. Add missing early-game weapon/ammo placements in container item lists (`world.js`) so firearms are obtainable.
6. Run `npm run build`, fix errors, start dev server on port 3002, capture 1440x900 screenshots via Playwright/SwiftShader, and iterate on visual/gameplay defects.
7. Inspect first gameplay frame: HUD visible, pharmacy/hospital/street visible, no menu/pause overlay, no blank canvas.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: still to create; central orchestration and render loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: completed city, props, interactables, quest points, safe zones, runtime updates.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: player controller, survival state, focus, pointer lock, camera.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/zombies.js`: enemy models, AI, damage, corpse loot, audio events.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/combat.js`: weapons, attacks, ammo, viewmodel rendering; contains noted integration bugs.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: DOM HUD, menus, panels, search/loot flow, quest display.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio engine and event sounds.

on:

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a playable first-person open-world zombie survival game inspired by Dying Light, emphasizing exploration, looting, and survival in an atmospheric abandoned city, using Three.js.

## Requirements
- Ultra-realistic 3D graphics; large explorable city with enterable houses, apartments, shops and hospitals.
- Search rooms, cupboards, drawers and containers for supplies.
- Multiple zombie types, realistic weapons/combat.
- Complete survival system: health, stamina, hunger, inventory.
- Day/night cycles, dynamic weather, realistic animations and immersive sound.
- First-person gameplay and atmospheric post-apocalyptic world.
- Exploration, looting and survival must be the main focus; world should feel dangerous, realistic and immersive.

## Decisions
- Self-contained Vite + Three.js 0.187 web game; fully procedural textures, geometry, and WebAudio assets (no external asset downloads).
- Title: **DEAD HOUR**, set in Harbor City quarantine zone; start time ~17:19 golden hour.
- Gameplay starts at `(18, 1.65, 3.8)` looking west down Harbor Avenue; hospital on right, pharmacy ahead.
- Start menu has one `PLAY` button (label-only text for capture regex compatibility), plus `HOW TO PLAY` and `SETTINGS`.
- Fonts loaded in `src/main.js` via `@fontsource/barlow-condensed` and `@fontsource/inter`.
- Quality strategy: merged geometry batches, post-processing bloom/grade, fog, procedural materials; currently `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = false` because no city geometry casts shadows.
- Loot flow: hover prompt → timed search → loot panel; inventory via Tab; start weapon `Worn Machete`.
- Quest: search Harbor Pharmacy for `antibiotics`, then deliver to The Old Laundry safehouse.
- Combat viewmodel uses separate `viewScene`/`viewCamera`; `combat.render()` now toggles `autoClear` off, calls `clearDepth`, renders overlay, then restores `autoClear`.
- Weapons/ammo placed in lootable containers: pistol + ammo in safehouse Weapon Locker; rifle in Military Crate; shotgun in Field Locker.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffold, `index.html`, complete HUD/menu/panel design in `src/styles.css`.
- All support modules implemented: `utils`, `textures`, `items`, `sky`, `world`, `player`, `zombies`, `inventory`, `combat`, `audio`, `ui`, `post`.
- Created `src/main.js` with renderer, scene/camera, module wiring, menu/Play flow, pause/pointer-lock handling, quest progression, weather/audio hooks, settings persistence, resize, frame loop, and weapon overlay.
- Added font imports to `main.js`.
- Fixed build/runtime texture bugs: added missing `dirtTextures()` export, defined missing `c` in sidewalk/concrete/plaster/brick/wood/wallpaper/tile/carpet texture functions, renamed duplicate asphalt noise variable to `base`.
- Fixed `combat.muzzleFlash` matrix update, `combat.meleeHit` condition lookup, and weapon-overlay overwrite issue.
- Changed Start button to label-only `PLAY` with CSS pseudo-element icons.
- Replaced invalid `ammo_cache` loot entry with pistol ammo.
- Added firearm placements to safehouse locker, military crate, field locker.
- `npm run build` succeeds (only chunk-size warning).
- Dev server running on port 3002; menu and gameplay screenshots captured successfully with no console errors.
- Dust particle size/opacity reduced in `world.js`; menu/game now render.

### Active
- Visual polish pass after first gameplay screenshot.
- Investigating excessive bright/blue sparkle aliasing across ground and market stall; suspect high-frequency procedural texture bright grain amplified by additive `lightPool` and bloom/chromatic aberration.
- Need to inspect/possibly fix `world.addGlow()` because it uses black `blobTexture()` multiplied by color under additive blending, likely making glow sprites invisible.

### Blocked
- None functionally; app builds and runs, but visual quality still needs iteration.

## Next Move
1. Diagnose sparkle/noise source by toggling suspect batches/materials (`lightPool`, `glass`, `windowPane`, decals) and inspecting close-up screenshots.
2. Reduce texture high-frequency bright speckles and/or lower `lightPool` additive intensity and bloom strength.
3. Fix `world.addGlow()` texture/color so street lights and quest/safehouse glows actually render.
4. Verify first gameplay frame at 1440x900: HUD, pharmacy/hospital/street, machete viewmodel, no menu/pause overlay, no blank canvas.
5. Test core gameplay: movement, door interaction, container search, loot panel, inventory, zombie combat, death/restart, pause/settings.
6. Verify quest flow: loot antibiotics → objective updates → deliver at Old Laundry → completion toast.
7. Check performance and visual quality on SwiftShader; tune quality defaults if needed.
8. Capture final menu/gameplay screenshots and run final build.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: central orchestration, render loop, quest, settings, input wiring.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: city generation, containers, quest points, atmosphere, dust, light pools, glow sprites.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/combat.js`: weapons, viewmodel overlay, melee/gun combat.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui.js`: HUD, menus, search/loot, inventory, quest display.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/textures.js`: all procedural textures; recent runtime fixes.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/player.js`: controller, survival stats, focus raycasts, pointer lock.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/zombies.js`: enemy models, AI, damage, corpse loot.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/sky.js`: day/night, weather, rain, sun/moon, environment.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/post.js`: bloom/grade composer, quality and render scale.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ambience and SFX.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/inventory.js`: item stacks, weight, equip, condition.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/items.js`: item registry, icons, loot tables.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: DOM structure and menu buttons.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles.css`: HUD/menu styling and PLAY pseudo-elements.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/`: captured menu/game/no-post images for visual inspection.

## Important Context
- Build command: `npm run build`; dev server: `npm run dev` on port 3002 (currently running in tmux session `dev`).
- No commits made; all work remains uncommitted in the working tree.
- `world.build()` sets `this.batches = null`; runtime `addContainer` works.
- Quest coordinates: pharmacy `(3,1.6,-9)`, safehouse `(-27,1.6,9.5)`, hospital `(27,1.6,-9)`.
- Player start `(18,0,3.8)`, yaw `PI/2`, eye `1.66` m.
- `world.safeZones` includes `The Old Laundry` at `(-27,14.5,r=5.2)`.
- Quest crate: Delivery Crate at `(5.9,-20.5)` with guaranteed `antibiotics`.
- `world.pointLights` culls to nearest ~7 lights.
- `GeoBatch` materials must be registered via `B.use(key, material)` before `build()`.
- `world.addGlow()` currently creates additive sprites with a black RGB blob texture; may need a white/alpha texture instead.
- Screenshot capture requires extended timeout (`page.screenshot({ timeout: 90000 })`) due to SwiftShader.
- Playwright Chromium was installed; `playwright-cli` open/resize/screenshot working.
- Game exposes `window.__deadHour` and `window.game` for debugging.
